items.name: Apache Ant
items.description: Java-based build automation tool that uses XML configuration files to define tasks for compiling, testing, and packaging software projects.

items.name: Azure DevOps
items.description: Microsoft suite of cloud services for software development teams, bundling source control, CI/CD pipelines, work item tracking, and artifact management.

items.name: Azure Pipelines
items.description: CI/CD service within Azure DevOps that automates building, testing, and deploying applications across multiple platforms and languages.

items.name: Bitbucket
items.description: Git repository hosting platform from Atlassian that supports code collaboration, pull requests, and built-in CI/CD pipelines, often paired with Jira.

items.name: BrowserStack
items.description: Cloud-based platform that lets teams test websites and mobile apps on real browsers and devices without maintaining local device labs.

items.name: CloudBees
items.description: Company offering enterprise DevOps and software delivery automation products, including managed Jenkins and CI/CD platforms for large organizations.

items.name: Concourse
items.description: Open-source continuous integration and delivery system that models workflows as pipelines of containerized tasks and resources.

items.name: Fastlane
items.description: Open-source toolset for automating the build, testing, and release process of iOS and Android mobile applications.

items.name: Git
items.description: Distributed version control system used to track changes in source code and coordinate collaborative software development across teams.

items.name: GitHub
items.description: Web-based hosting service for Git repositories that provides tools for code collaboration, pull requests, issue tracking, and project management.

items.name: GitHub Actions
items.description: CI/CD feature built into GitHub that lets teams define automated workflows for building, testing, and deploying code triggered by repository events.

items.name: GitLab
items.description: Web-based DevOps platform combining Git repository hosting with issue tracking, CI/CD, and project management in a single application.

items.name: GitLab CI/CD
items.description: Built-in continuous integration and deployment feature of GitLab that automates pipelines for building, testing, and releasing code.

items.name: GoCD
items.description: Open-source continuous delivery server designed for modeling complex build and deployment pipelines with dependency tracking and visualization.

items.name: Gulp
items.description: JavaScript-based task runner used to automate repetitive front-end development tasks such as minification, compilation, and file watching.

items.name: Jenkins
items.description: Open-source automation server used to build continuous integration and delivery pipelines, extensible through a large plugin ecosystem.

items.name: JFrog Artifactory
items.description: Universal binary repository manager for storing, versioning, and distributing build artifacts and dependencies across many package formats.

items.name: Make
items.description: Build automation tool that reads Makefiles describing dependencies between files to compile and link programs efficiently.

items.name: Newman
items.description: Command-line tool for running and automating Postman API test collections, often used in CI pipelines for API testing.

items.name: Octopus Deploy
items.description: Deployment automation tool that manages application releases and orchestrates deployments across multiple environments and servers.

items.name: Team Foundation Server
items.description: Microsoft's on-premises application lifecycle management platform providing source control, build automation, and work item tracking, later rebranded as Azure DevOps Server.

items.name: TeamCity
items.description: CI/CD server from JetBrains used to automate building, testing, and deploying software projects.

items.name: Visual Studio App Center
items.description: Cloud-based service from Microsoft for building, testing, distributing, and monitoring mobile and desktop applications throughout their lifecycle.

items.name: AWS CDK
items.description: Framework that lets developers define cloud infrastructure using familiar programming languages, which is then synthesized into CloudFormation templates for deployment.

items.name: AWS CloudFormation
items.description: AWS service for provisioning and managing cloud resources using declarative JSON or YAML templates, enabling infrastructure as code.

items.name: Azure Resource Manager Templates
items.description: JSON-based declarative templates used to define and deploy Azure resources in a consistent, repeatable way.

items.name: Bicep
items.description: Domain-specific language for deploying Azure resources declaratively, offering simpler syntax than raw ARM JSON templates while compiling down to them.

items.name: Packer
items.description: Tool for creating identical machine images for multiple platforms (cloud, virtualization, containers) from a single source configuration.

items.name: Pulumi
items.description: Infrastructure as code platform that lets teams define and manage cloud resources using general-purpose programming languages instead of a dedicated DSL.

items.name: Terraform
items.description: Infrastructure as code tool that uses a declarative configuration language to provision and manage resources across many cloud and on-premises providers.

items.name: Ansible
items.description: Agentless automation tool that uses YAML-based playbooks to handle configuration management, application deployment, and orchestration tasks.

items.name: Puppet
items.description: Configuration management tool that uses a declarative language to automate the provisioning, configuration, and maintenance of infrastructure at scale.

items.name: Amazon ECS
items.description: AWS container orchestration service for deploying, managing, and scaling Docker containers without needing to manage the underlying cluster software.

items.name: Amazon EKS
items.description: Managed service for running Kubernetes clusters on AWS without needing to install and operate the Kubernetes control plane.

items.name: Azure Container Apps
items.description: Serverless hosting service on Azure for running containerized applications and microservices without managing underlying infrastructure or orchestration directly.

items.name: Docker
items.description: Platform for building, packaging, and running applications in lightweight, portable containers that bundle code and dependencies together.

items.name: Docker Compose
items.description: Tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications using a single YAML configuration file to specify services, networks, and volumes.

items.name: Helm
items.description: Package manager for Kubernetes that uses charts to define, install, and upgrade complex applications and their dependencies.

items.name: Kubernetes
items.description: Open-source platform for automating the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications across clusters of machines.

items.name: Microsoft Hyper-V
items.description: Native hypervisor built into Windows for creating and managing virtual machines, enabling multiple operating systems to run on a single physical host.

items.name: OpenShift
items.description: Enterprise Kubernetes platform from Red Hat that adds developer and operational tooling on top of Kubernetes for building and deploying containerized applications.
